witness_description: No certified witness. The sweep finds the unresolved candidate U={0,1,2,3,4,5}, M={{0,1,2},{3,4,5}}, and B={{0,1,3},{0,2,3},{0,3,4}}: its three source sets give three parallel edges on two vertices and are not a packing, while M is globally optimal. Assigning each source set weight 1/3 gives positive exact weights, but feasibility cannot be certified from the supplied data.
refutation_explanation: The source quote never defines the constraints of the intersecting-family LP. Consequently the required hypothesis that x is feasible is not finitely checkable without inventing an absent definition. The bounded sweep exposes a concrete obstruction to the asserted packing implication, but it cannot certify that obstruction as a counterexample to the full claim.
search_space: Exhaustively swept all 8,160 pairs (M,B) on U={0,1,2,3,4,5}, where M is an unordered pair of disjoint 3-subsets and B is a 3-element subfamily of the remaining 3-subsets; for each pair, all four X subsets of M and all 32 subfamilies of C=M∪B were checked.
